body:
Surfaced by the Codex review of #465 (the M4 stateless-gateway blueprint).

## The gap
`Gateway` mints inode and chunk IDs from **per-process `AtomicU64` counters** (`crates/server/src/lib.rs` `next_inode`/`next_chunk`), seeded once at startup by `recover()` from `metadata::high_water_marks` and then advanced with `fetch_add`. This is safe for **one** gateway process (the code comment says so explicitly: "in-process counter for the single-process gateway, one process, not a multi-writer cluster").

It is **not** safe for two or more gateway processes against the same fleet: both seed from the same high-water mark and independently `fetch_add`, so they mint the **same** next inode/chunk id. The create-commit CAS rejects the losing inode, but the **chunk fragments are written to the D servers before that commit**, under the colliding chunk id — so the second gateway overwrites the first object's fragments (data loss).

Note the CLI path already uses the CAS-backed `meta:next_inode` allocator (`alloc_inode`, M4.4/#255); the **gateway does not** — it uses the in-process counter.

## Why it matters
The M4 first-deployment blueprint's "one shared front door, N gateways, no LB affinity, plain round-robin" property (from #454) depends on this. Until the gateway allocates IDs in a cluster-coordinated way, **only a single active gateway is safe** (active/standby, not active/active). #465 is being corrected to say exactly that and to point here.

## Fix options
- Gateway adopts the CAS-backed `meta:next_inode` allocator (as the CLI does) for inodes, and a cluster-safe chunk-id scheme.
- Or random/uncoordinated chunk ids per ADR-0019 (the "later refinement" the code comment names) + CAS inode allocation.
- Either way, add a conformance/DST property that two gateways never mint a colliding id under contention.

Not required for the single-gateway first deployment; this gates **multi-gateway** scale-out / HA on the S3 front door.

Refs #454 (gateway composition), #465 (blueprint), #364 (finding 1: restart id-replay), ADR-0019 (random chunk ids reserved).

milestone.description: Step 2. Swap embedded redb for distributed TiKV behind the unchanged MetadataStore trait; multi-key atomic directory ops hold under the distributed store. Completes the single-zone data plane — a soft stopping point, not the release: the ★ Step-2 release point is M8 (proposal 0013 implementation arc, supersedes 0002). Plan: proposal 0015 (supersedes 0007; acceptance PR #417); tracker #201; first-deployment gate #367.

title: Gateway: cluster-coordinated ID allocation so multiple gateways are safe (per-process AtomicU64 today)
